title: Flo Alternatives in Nigeria: Four Period Trackers Compared
description: Compare four Flo alternatives for Nigerian women trying to conceive. See reminders, prices, sign-up and what each tracker lets you do with your dates.
share: If you want an alternative to Flo in Nigeria, this comparison shows what four period trackers let you do, what they cost and where they keep your dates.
kicker: For Nigerian women who want another option beside Flo
answer: If you want to see fertile days without signing up, choose Wholesome Girlies. If you want reminders and years of saved entries, choose Period Calendar. Clue gives you expert-written guides, while Ovia can stay with you through pregnancy and postpartum. No app here can tell you the exact day you ovulate from dates alone.

picks.name: Wholesome Girlies
picks.label: Start without signing up
picks.suits: Choose it if you want your dates on your phone, questions to print for the clinic and a checklist to send your partner.
picks.does: Open six fertility tools, including the Period Tracker and Ovulation Calculator. You can also buy The Trying-to-Conceive Blueprint.
picks.watch: You cannot note symptoms. Reminders go into your own phone calendar when you tap Add to my calendar. The calculator counts 14 days back from your next period and cannot detect ovulation.
picks.price: The tools need no card. The Blueprint is ₦5,700 early-bird (₦13,700 standard), paid once. Buyers abroad pay $12 early-bird ($27 standard).
picks.rating: Not in the app stores. Open it here, or add the Girlies app to your home screen.

picks.name: Clue
picks.label: Read expert-written guides
picks.suits: Choose it if you want expert-written guides and do not mind advice that was not written for Nigeria.
picks.does: Track your cycle with an app from Berlin. Clue says it does not sell your data to advertisers.
picks.watch: Forecasts need the Plus tier. Clue ranks 46 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart.
picks.price: Clue Plus on the Nigerian App Store runs from ₦1,500 (about $1) to ₦12,900 (about $10).

picks.name: Period Calendar
picks.label: Get reminders and keep years
picks.suits: Choose it if you want reminders and want to keep years of period entries in one app.
picks.does: Track your cycle and get reminders. It ranks 2 in the Nigerian App Store Health and Fitness chart and first in Nigerian Google Play search for period tracker.
picks.watch: Google Play marks it as containing ads, and reviews mention ads and upgrade pop-ups.
picks.price: In-app purchases on the Nigerian App Store run from ₦500 (about $0.40) for 7 days of Premium to ₦69,900 (about $52) for Pro: Period Calendar.

picks.name: Ovia
picks.label: Keep one app for later
picks.suits: Choose it if you want the same app for fertility, pregnancy and postpartum.
picks.does: See a daily fertility score and switch to pregnancy, postpartum or menopause mode. Its listing also says it has over 2,000 articles.
picks.watch: It has in-app purchases on both stores. Ovuline makes it, and the company is now Ovia Health by Labcorp.
picks.price: Google Play Nigeria lists purchases inside the app from ₦4,270 (about $3) to ₦29,000 (about $22).

reviews.title: Why women look elsewhere: what they say about Flo

why: Women reviewing Flo, Clue and Period Calendar often want to see the price before paying. They also mention upgrade pop-ups, losing dates when they change phone and advice that does not fit where they live. Our Nigerian samples are too small to show how common each concern is.

faq.q: Is there a Flo alternative that needs no account?
faq.a: The Wholesome Girlies Period Tracker and Ovulation Calculator open with no sign-in. Period Calendar's App Store listing says you can use it without an account, Flo has an Anonymous Mode that needs no name or email, and Clue offers an account at no cost.

faq.q: Which alternative is best for trying to conceive?
faq.a: Choose Wholesome Girlies if you want clinic questions and a partner checklist. Choose Clue for expert-written guides. Choose Period Calendar for reminders and years of saved dates.

faq.q: Do these apps predict ovulation accurately?
faq.a: No app on this page can detect ovulation from dates alone. A Journal of Medical Internet Research analysis of 7,043 tracked cycles found ovulation does not sit reliably at the midpoint. Take your last three or four period dates to a clinician.

doctor: See a doctor after twelve months of trying, or six months if you are over 35. See one sooner if your cycles are very irregular, shorter than 21 days or longer than 35, or have stopped. Take your last three or four period dates with you.

disclaimer.strong: This page compares apps. It cannot tell you when you will conceive.
disclaimer.rest: A calendar predicts and does not detect. It is educational, not medical advice, and no clinician has reviewed it yet.
